General guidance from the offline library:
Inspecting a crop problem before treatment
Confirm the crop identity first. Record when symptoms began, how they progressed, and which plants or plant parts are affected. Inspect the whole plant and its surroundings, not only one leaf. Take both whole-plant and close-up pictures. Ask about watering, site history and recent changes. Similar symptoms can have different causes; a general description or a single leaf photo is insufficient for a confident diagnosis. Identify the cause before selecting a treatment.

Please confirm the crop or animal, describe the marks or symptoms you can see, and say how long they have been present. This is general reference guidance, not a photo diagnosis.
